item.title: Brigid and the Cloak
item.description: A bedtime story about Saint Brigid of Kildare, who asked a king for only as much land as her cloak could cover, and the cloak that went on spreading. Told as the old tradition tells it, with a note for grown-ups on what is history and what is legend. For ages 3 to 8, about ten minutes read aloud. Her feast day is the 1st of February. Setting: Ireland, in the time of the old kings, about fifteen hundred years ago. Read the full text at https://example.invalid/hearth-and-horizon/brigid-and-the-cloak.html. Written by Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic; read by a synthetic voice. CC BY-SA 4.0.

item.title: Kevin and the Blackbird
item.description: A bedtime story about Saint Kevin of Glendalough, who was praying with his hand held out of a window when a blackbird laid an egg in it, and who stayed still until the chick hatched. Told as the old legend tells it, with a note for grown-ups on what is history and what is legend. For ages 3 to 8, about nine minutes read aloud. His feast day is the 3rd of June. Setting: Glendalough, the valley of two lakes in the Wicklow mountains, Ireland, about fourteen hundred years ago. Read the full text at https://example.invalid/hearth-and-horizon/kevin-and-the-blackbird.html. Written by Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic; read by a synthetic voice. CC BY-SA 4.0.
